subject.title: message_tool_only: one-shot delivery reminder loses to recency over long tool chains, turns end in withheld finals

question: For long `message_tool_only` turns that end with a plain private final, should OpenClaw add periodic in-turn delivery reminders, a bounded post-withhold recovery nudge, or both?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes prompt budget, retry semantics, duplicate-delivery risk, and the privacy boundary for private finals, so automation should not choose the permanent behavior alone.

options.title: Combine Reminder And Recovery
options.body: Add a fixed-size reminder after bounded tool activity and coordinate it with one-shot stranded-final recovery for substantive private finals.

options.title: Recovery Only
options.body: Use the stranded-final recovery path to repair missed finals after the model fails, without adding more prompt traffic during long tool chains.

options.title: Reminder Only
options.body: Refresh the delivery instruction during long turns but leave withheld-final retry or diagnostic behavior to separate recovery work.

recommendation.title: Combine Reminder And Recovery
recommendation.body: Add a fixed-size reminder after bounded tool activity and coordinate it with one-shot stranded-final recovery for substantive private finals.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the private-final warning path, source-delivery privacy contract, and active recovery PR history where this handle is the clearest routing signal.
